pre-commit.description: Renovate leaves the pre-commit manager disabled by default, so a repository that pins its hooks by rev gets no updates for them at all. Six skill repositories were found sitting on skill-repo-skill v1.22.0 while the fleet ran v1.37.0, still enforcing a SKILL.md word cap the fleet had replaced with a body-line cap in August 2026.

gomod.description: Renovate runs go mod tidy only when postUpdateOptions asks for it, so a Go module update leaves the previous version's checksums in go.sum. A repository whose pre-commit check runs go mod tidy then refuses every commit until someone tidies by hand: in netresearch/ofelia that cleanup was needed three times, and open Renovate pull requests in ldap-manager, ldap-selfservice-password-changer, raybeam and simple-ldap-go carried the same stale lines in October 2026.

pep621.description: Renovate's pep621 manager tracks only the dependencies a pyproject.toml declares, so a transitive pin in uv.lock is never raised and lockFileMaintenance, which would refresh it, is off by default. In netresearch/t3x-nr-llm certifi, filelock and setuptools each stayed on a version an advisory lists until the lock was re-run by hand, and the Renovate run after the four filelock/setuptools alerts of October 2026 opened no pull request. agent-rules-skill and coding_agent_cli_toolset carry uv.lock files with the same gap. Weekly lock maintenance runs uv lock --upgrade, inside the constraints pyproject.toml sets.

packageRules.description: Deny-list compromised axios versions (supply chain attack 2026-03-31)

Automerge everything that does not change what we depend on. lockFileMaintenance only refreshes transitive pins inside the existing constraints, and a rollback returns to a version that already ran here, usually because the newer one was withdrawn - holding either back helps nobody. stabilityDays and internalChecksFilter above still apply, so nothing merges before it has aged and its checks are green.

A Docker digest update has no release age to wait for. Renovate takes the age from the tag, and a tag such as php:8.5-alpine is pushed again whenever the publisher rebuilds it - php:8.5-alpine and composer:2 were both pushed on 2026-10-22 between 01:00 and 03:15 UTC - so the age measures the last rebuild, not a release. Where the registry returns no timestamp at all, minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour timestamp-required holds the update for good. Either way internalChecksFilter strict drops it from the branch: netresearch/phpbu-docker received no digest of its php base image after 2026-07-13, while its dependency dashboard listed the update. The digest still names the same tag the repository already chose, so this rule lifts the age only for digest updates; new versions keep the stabilityDays above.

Mark what a human has to look at, so machinery downstream can tell it apart. A major can break callers; a replacement swaps the dependency for a differently named successor, so the identity of what we depend on changes. Neither is covered by the automerge rule above, but that is a decision only Renovate knows about: nothing on the pull request says which update type it carries, and the auto-merge workflow in netresearch/.github consequently merged them anyway, overriding this policy. The label makes the distinction visible to anything that reads the pull request.

A TYPO3 major is a framework-support decision, not an update decision. The constraint in composer.json states which core versions an extension is built and tested against, so widening it is a release-planning act that needs a CI matrix cell, a version sweep across ext_emconf.php, guides.xml and the documentation, and someone who owns the outcome. Renovate splits that one decision into one pull request per typo3/cms-* package - t3x-contexts_geolocation got four on 2026-09-18, each mergeable on its own, and merging any of them would have claimed v14 support nobody decided on. It also gets it wrong inside a major that IS supported: t3x-nr-passkeys-be#145 proposed adding || ^14.0 next to an existing ^14.3, lowering the floor to a version that was never built against. The update stays visible on the dependency dashboard and can be started from there once the support decision has been made. vulnerabilityAlerts above uses force and overrides this, and patches and minors inside the supported majors are untouched.

A PHPUnit major follows the framework, not the code. In a TYPO3 extension typo3/testing-framework decides which PHPUnit runs: 8.x accepts ^10.1 || ^11.0 and serves TYPO3 12/13, 9.5 and later add ^13.0.2 but serve only TYPO3 13/14. t3x-contexts_wurfl#59 proposed adding || ^13.0 to an extension that still claims TYPO3 12, where no installable testing-framework accepts PHPUnit 13. So the PHPUnit major is decided together with the supported core range, through the rule above. The same holds for other framework projects, where the framework's test suite pins PHPUnit. saschaegerer/phpstan-typo3 follows the core the same way: 2.x requires typo3/cms-core ^13.4.3, 3.1 requires ^14.0, so t3x-nr-llm-compat#11 silently moved its solver test environment from TYPO3 13.4 to 14.3. vulnerabilityAlerts above uses force and overrides this.

Guzzle majors move as one stack. guzzlehttp/oauth-subscriber 0.9.6 requires guzzle ^7.15.5 and 1.0.1 requires guzzle ^8.1 with psr7 ^3.1 and promises ^3.0.2, so neither major resolves on its own. Split into one pull request per package, timetracker#812 (guzzle 8) and #813 (oauth-subscriber 1) both failed composer.lock resolution and only a hand-made combined update (#836) could land them. One group gives Renovate a single composer update over every guzzlehttp/* major at once.
